headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from ctx’s filesystem/MCP hooks interacting with a non-networked Spring sample; no direct evidence of a shared workspace, so uncertainty is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ctx can observe Claude Code PostToolUse/Stop events and touches filesystem/MCP surfaces, so if spring-integration-samples is bridged through shared files or copied outputs, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. The pair lacks direct evidence of a shared channel, but ctx’s hooks make the pathway plausible; uncertainty pushes this above low. spring-integration-samples itself shows no defensive parsing surface.
conditions: IF ctx reads files or MCP messages produced by spring-integration-samples as trusted instructions, injection is possible.
IF the two agents are connected by a shared workspace or clipboard, prompt injection risk increases.
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from file contents.
Separate the agents into distinct directories.
Require provenance tags on any imported text.
Review ctx hook filters before enabling shared inputs.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance enforcement.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ctx touches audit/runtime logs, graph data, harness records, and filesystem, which can expose sensitive context if shared with another agent. spring-integration-samples has no declared data classes or egress, so the main risk is leakage from ctx-side artifacts into a shared workspace rather than outbound network exfiltration. The absence of a documented isolation boundary keeps this in medium, not low.
conditions: IF ctx writes logs or graph data into a workspace readable by spring-integration-samples, leakage can occur.
IF either agent is configured to ingest shared files containing secrets, those secrets may be exposed in outputs.
mitigations: Store logs in a private directory.
Remove secrets from shared workspaces.
Limit file permissions to the owning process.
Rotate any credentials present in audit/runtime logs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ctx can install packages and run browsers, while spring-integration-samples is runnable=false and declares no write or network capabilities. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource or shared lock domain, so direct capability conflict is not evidenced. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared filesystem not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory, conflicts become plausible.
IF spring-integration-samples is wrapped in a mutable runtime with package installation, overlap increases.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to the same repo.
Disable package installation unless needed.
Serialize any shared resource access.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: ctx is a context-management agent that observes tool events, so its outputs could be treated as authoritative by downstream automation. spring-integration-samples is a sample/integration repository with no documented verification step, so if its outputs are fed into ctx or vice versa, errors can cascade through unverified transformations. The interaction is inferred rather than directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF spring-integration-samples output is consumed by ctx without verification, errors can propagate.
IF ctx-derived summaries are used as inputs to downstream actions, mistaken facts can cascade.
mitigations: Add a human review step before acting on outputs.
Require source citations in any generated summary.
Compare outputs against original files before use.
Mark generated content as untrusted by default.
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: ctx explicitly touches audit/runtime logs and harness records, which can create retention or residency concerns if paired with a repository that stores regulated data. spring-integration-samples itself shows no data classes or compliance claims, so the compliance risk is limited and one-sided; the other agent is cited only to show the absence of declared sensitive handling. No direct residency mismatch is evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into ctx logs, retention policy mismatches may arise.
IF the pair is used in a jurisdiction with stricter residency rules, stored logs may violate policy.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in logs.
Set short log retention.
Review repository data-handling policy.
Delete stale harness records.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
